09:00.headline: Top travel team or every-day reps?
09:00.topic: Debate: elite travel team with fewer innings vs solid team with full playing time

graphic.headline: Top travel team or *every-day reps?*
graphic.ask: No wrong answer. *Which would you pick?*

09:00.facebook_caption_draft:
Baseball parents, here's one we hear a lot.

Your son can join the top-ranked travel team, with bigger events and more college coaches watching, but he'd share time and may sit some innings. Or he can stay with a solid team where he plays every game.

The case for the top team: tougher competition and a real read on how he stacks up.
The case for staying: more at-bats, more innings, more game video and more room to develop.

Which would you choose, and what made the difference for your family? Share in the comments.

See what the numbers say about his best college fit:
https://baseballfuture.com

13:00.headline: Corner infielders: what to build
13:00.topic: Player development for 1B/3B: game power, hands/feet, arm accuracy, at-bat plan; baseline and retest

graphic.headline: Corner infielders: *what to build*
items: Power that shows up in games
An accurate arm on the move

13:00.facebook_caption_draft:
If your son plays first or third, this winter is a good time to look past batting practice.

College coaches expect corner infielders to hit, but they also watch the rest of his game:
- Power that shows up in games
- Soft hands and quick feet around the bag
- An accurate arm, including throws on the move
- A plan in every at-bat against good pitching

Pick one or two to work on, write down where he starts, and retest later so you can see real progress.

What's your corner infielder working on this offseason?
